title: Dependency injection registration mismatch

sourceOfTruth.rule: Use constructor signatures from the installed DLL and startup error text to verify required registrations.

symptoms: Build succeeds but application startup fails because a service cannot be resolved.
Constructor/generic changes compiled but DI still points to the old registration shape.
investigation: Read the exact startup error and missing service type.
Find the constructor that requires the missing dependency.
Search registration files, Startup.cs, Program.cs, and CommonDIRegistrations.cs.
Check whether the service is generic and requires matching type arguments.
patchRules: Register missing dependencies with the same lifetime pattern used by adjacent Core services.
Update open-generic or closed-generic registration arity to match the decompiled service contract.
Keep constructor and DI registration fixes in the same patch batch where possible.
antiPatterns: Do not change service lifetimes arbitrarily.
Do not register a concrete type if the existing convention uses interfaces.
Do not hide missing dependency errors with service locator fallbacks.

commands: run application startup or the project's existing smoke test when available
successCriteria: The missing-service startup error is gone.
No new DI error appears for the same constructor family.
